clue.text: Perfect motorsport backing number one in Monaco

parts.note: F1, Formula One, with the 1 read as the letter I

indicators.note: backing means the word for a number is read from right to left

parts.note: ten is a number
une is French for one, the language spoken in Monaco

explanation.surface: Formula One cars racing round Monaco, with a driver backing the top contender.
explanation.walkthrough: The digit 1 in F1 is read as the letter I, a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: To fine-tune something is to make small adjustments until it is just right, a verb synonym for perfect.

clue.text: Bored of extremely forgettable party

indicators.note: extremely asks for the extreme letters, the first and last, of the following word

parts.note: the first and last letters of forgettable
the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Someone tired of a party they would rather forget.
explanation.walkthrough: The DUP is a Northern Irish political party.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fed up is an informal idiom for being weary and dissatisfied, close in sense to bored.

clue.text: Island's optimistic with hospital being replaced by modern architect initially

indicators.note: being replaced by tells us to swap the hospital word out and put the modern word in its place

parts.note: sanguine means cheerfully optimistic
a san, short for sanatorium, is a hospital or sick bay
new means modern

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of the word architect

parts.note: the first letter of architect

explanation.surface: An upbeat island whose hospital has been rebuilt by a modern architect.
explanation.walkthrough: SAN, short for sanatorium, is a crossword staple for hospital; here it sits at the start of a word meaning optimistic.
explanation.definitionFit: New Guinea is a large island in the Pacific north of Australia, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: That lot record 6 rides here?

parts.note: them is a pronoun for that lot of people
an EP is an extended-play record
6 refers to the answer at 6-down, a box or chest; the Ark of the Covenant was a chest

explanation.surface: Those people put on a record while six of them go on fairground rides.
explanation.walkthrough: The 6 is a cross-reference to 6-down, whose answer means box; an ark is a chest, as in the Biblical Ark of the Covenant.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme park is an amusement venue full of rides, so the question mark flags a definition by location.

clue.text: Heard about any tea dance after game

indicators.note: heard says to listen to the words that follow rather than read them, here roughly the sound of the letters

parts.note: said aloud, any tea sounds like the letter names N and T run together with an E sound between
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Someone audibly fussing over tea and dancing once the match is over.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, any tea runs together as the names of the letters N and T around an E sound, giving the first part.
explanation.definitionFit: Netball is a team sport played with a ball and high hoops, widely played in Britain and the Commonwealth, so it is a game.

clue.text: Small motor — a black Beetle

parts.note: motor is an informal word for a car
taken as written

explanation.surface: A small car, such as a black Volkswagen Beetle.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital B on Beetle suggests the Volkswagen car, but the definition is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarab is a dung beetle held sacred in ancient Egypt, so it is a specific kind of the insect.

clue.text: Estimated two taps should open box

indicators.note: to open something is to come at its start, so the tap letters go at the front

parts.note: a sink's taps are marked C and H, for cold and hot
EST is the standard abbreviation for estimated

explanation.surface: Two quick taps on a box ought to make it open, as a rough guess.
explanation.walkthrough: EST is the usual abbreviation for estimated.
explanation.definitionFit: A chest is a large sturdy container with a lid, a synonym for box.

clue.text: Donor-insemination nurses wash

indicators.note: nurses in the sense of holding or cradling, so the answer is held within the run of letters

parts.note: the answer runs across the join, from the last letter of Donor into the start of insemination

explanation.surface: Nurses at a fertility clinic washing up after donor insemination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nurses' looks like the people in the scene, but it is a verb meaning holds.
explanation.definitionFit: To rinse is to wash lightly in clean water, a close synonym.

clue.text: Internet mostly capturing electronic pulse

indicators.note: capturing means the shortened word surrounds the letter for electronic
mostly means almost all of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: broadband is a high-speed internet connection

explanation.surface: An internet connection that mostly picks up an electronic pulse signal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' sounds electrical next to internet and electronic, but here it means an edible seed.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulses are the edible seeds of legumes such as lentils and beans, and the broad bean is one of them.

clue.text: Sedate city with royal house not spoken about

indicators.note: about means the trimmed residence goes around the city letters
not tells us the spoken word is to be removed

parts.note: Balmoral is the royal family's castle in Scotland
oral means spoken
EC is the postcode for the City of London

explanation.surface: A calm town where the royal residence is never mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: Balmoral Castle in Aberdeenshire is a royal residence; take away the word for spoken and what is left wraps round EC.
explanation.definitionFit: To becalm is to make calm or still, so it serves as a verb synonym for sedate.

clue.text: Ultimately had to swallow his pride and work with Rod?

indicators.note: ultimately picks the ultimate, or last, letter of each of the five words that follow, not just the first

parts.note: last letter of had
last letter of to
last letter of swallow
last letter of his
last letter of pride

explanation.surface: A man who finally had to swallow his pride and team up with a colleague called Rod.
explanation.walkthrough: Rod with its capital letter looks like a man's name, but it is a divining rod.
explanation.definitionFit: Dowsing is searching for underground water with a forked divining stick, so to dowse is to work with one.

clue.text: Other tune composed in addition

indicators.note: composed in the sense of arranged or put together, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: the nine letters of these two words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A second melody written as an extra piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereunto is an archaic word meaning besides or to that, an old-fashioned synonym of the phrase.

clue.text: Discharge energy following power cut

indicators.note: following places the discharge and energy letters after the power letter

parts.note: to run is to discharge, as a tap or a sore runs

explanation.surface: A power cut lets loose a burst of stored energy.
explanation.definitionFit: To prune is to trim back a plant, so it is a synonym of cut.

clue.text: Two articles embracing equality with papers revealing systemic racism?

indicators.note: embracing means the two articles hold the equality word between them

parts.note: a and the, the indefinite and definite articles
par means equality, as in on a par
ID, identity papers

explanation.surface: Two newspaper articles about equality, with documents exposing racism built into the system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles' suggests newspaper pieces next to papers, but here they are the grammatical words a and the.
explanation.definitionFit: Apartheid was South Africa's legal system of racial segregation; the question mark marks it as one example of institutional discrimination.

clue.text: Somehow clone amphibian with gills essentially for oxygen — it needs flippers

indicators.note: somehow means the letters are put together in some other way
for means one letter stands in for the other, so the oxygen letter is swapped out

parts.note: the fourteen letters of these words are the fodder, before one letter is swapped

indicators.note: essentially picks the essence, the central letter, of the word gills

parts.note: the middle letter of gills

explanation.surface: Cloning a gilled amphibian, a newt perhaps, that would need flippers to swim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flippers' suggests a swimming creature, but they are the paddles of an arcade game.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinball machine is an arcade game in which the player keeps a ball in play with two flippers.

clue.text: Sally Army top in church revenue

indicators.note: a sally is a sortie or excursion, so the letters break out into a new order

parts.note: the nine letters of these three words are the fodder

explanation.surface: The Salvation Army's top people collect the takings in church.
explanation.walkthrough: Sally Army is British slang for the Salvation Army, which makes the surface read smoothly.
explanation.definitionFit: Patrimony can mean the endowment or estate belonging to a church, its inherited income.

clue.text: See 14
Judge boring religious office making pub empty bar

indicators.note: making means the pub letters turn into the emptied bar

parts.note: a caliphate is the office of a caliph, an Islamic ruler
PH is the map abbreviation for public house

indicators.note: empty means the inside of the word bar is cleared out, keeping its outer letters

parts.note: the outer letters of bar, with its middle removed

explanation.surface: Sitting through a dull church role while turning the pub into an empty bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' reads as dull, but it belongs to the definition: the bore is the inside diameter of a gun barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: To calibrate a gun is to measure the diameter of its bore, so it means to gauge a boring.

clue.text: Traveller is repetitive when describing home

indicators.note: describing in its old sense of drawing around, so the repetitive word encloses home

parts.note: iterant means repeating
in, at home

explanation.surface: A traveller keeps repeating themselves when talking about home.
explanation.definitionFit: An itinerant is someone who travels from place to place, so the noun is a synonym of traveller.

clue.text: Perhaps Tom is inspired by Sri Lankan hero — I'm hugely grateful

indicators.note: inspired in its literal sense of breathed in, so the actor is taken inside the hero

parts.note: a Tamil lion, a brave fighter from Sri Lanka's Tamil people
Tom Hanks is one Tom, the American actor, signalled by perhaps

explanation.surface: An actor drawing inspiration from a Sri Lankan hero and gushing with gratitude.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tamils are a people of northern Sri Lanka.
explanation.definitionFit: Thanks a million is an idiom for heartfelt gratitude, matching the exclamation.

clue.text: Brute's returning all glam in acrylic trousers

indicators.note: returning means the hidden letters are read in the opposite direction
trousers as a verb, meaning pockets, so the letters are held inside the phrase

parts.note: the letters sit across the end of glam, all of in and the start of acrylic

explanation.surface: A brute goes back to wearing glam acrylic trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trousers' looks like the clothing, but it is a verb meaning pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal is a beast, and a brute is a beast or a savage person.

clue.text: See 18
Graduate incorporating representative colour

indicators.note: incorporating means the degree letters take in the representative

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate
an agent acts as a representative

explanation.surface: A graduate takes on a representative to promote their colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Magenta is a purplish-red shade, so it is an example of a colour.

clue.text: Segregating bar area is offensive

indicators.note: bar as a verb meaning exclude, so the area letter is left out

parts.note: insulating means isolating or keeping apart

explanation.surface: Keeping a bar area segregated is offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a pub alongside area, but it is a verb meaning exclude.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulting remarks are rude and hurtful, so the word is a synonym of offensive.

clue.text: Runner taking tablet before final of marathon should make bundle

indicators.note: before puts the runner part ahead of the final letter
taking means the runner takes the tablet inside it

parts.note: a ski is a runner, as on a sledge
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

indicators.note: final of picks the last letter of marathon

parts.note: the last letter of marathon

explanation.surface: A marathon runner popping a pill before the finish line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests the marathon athlete, but it is a ski.
explanation.definitionFit: A skein is a loosely coiled length of yarn, a bundle of thread.

clue.text: ULEZ assessed in prime locations for legal agreement

indicators.note: counting through both words, keep only the letters at prime-numbered positions: second, third, fifth, seventh and eleventh

parts.note: positions two and three are the inner pair of ULEZ
positions five, seven and eleven fall on the first, third and seventh letters of assessed

explanation.surface: London's clean-air charge assessed at sites across the capital under a formal agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: ULEZ is London's Ultra Low Emission Zone charge. 'Prime locations' sounds like estate-agent speak but means the prime-numbered letter positions.
explanation.definitionFit: A lease is a contract granting use of property for a set period, a kind of legal agreement.

clue.text: Better holiday

explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like an adjective, but it is a verb, to outdo.
explanation.definitionFit: You break a record by surpassing it, and a break is also a short holiday.

clue.text: Dictator's demand for massage

indicators.note: a dictator here is someone dictating aloud, so the word is as heard

parts.note: a need is a demand or requirement

explanation.surface: A tyrant insisting on a massage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dictator' suggests a tyrant, but here it is someone dictating words aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: To knead is to work and press with the hands, as a masseur does, so it is a verb synonym.

clue.text: Once more on account of a profit

parts.note: over can mean because of, as in a row over money
taken as written
a gain is a profit

explanation.surface: Repeating a transaction because it turned a profit.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something over again is doing it a second time, an idiom for repetition.

clue.text: Shocked seeing space in hospital department

indicators.note: in places the space word inside the department letters

parts.note: A&E, accident and emergency
a gap is a space

explanation.surface: Someone stunned at finding room in a busy hospital department.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E, accident and emergency, is the British name for a hospital's emergency room.
explanation.definitionFit: Agape means wide open-mouthed with amazement, as a stunned person is.

clue.text: Terms of my ASBO mean I'd be better off, far away

indicators.note: terms in the sense of terminations: the last letter of each of the six words that follow, not just the first

parts.note: last letter of my
last letter of ASBO
last letter of mean
last letter of I'd
last letter of be
last letter of better

explanation.surface: Someone under a court order reckons they would be better off somewhere far away.
explanation.walkthrough: An ASBO was a British antisocial behaviour order; 'terms' reads as its conditions but means word endings.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonder is an old or dialect word for over there, at a distance.

clue.text: Moaned as metal end melted

indicators.note: metal that has melted loses its shape and is recast, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: the eight letters of these words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A worker groaning as the end of a piece of metal melted away.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamented means expressed grief or complaint aloud, a synonym of moaned.
